capabilities: Encrypt folder trees recursively with AES-256-GCM
Unlock folders with a password for temporary session access
Auto-lock folders on background, exit, or inactivity timeout
Generate and back up a recovery key
Permanently remove encryption once all files are plaintext
extras: Anonymous telemetry via OpenPanel is enabled by default and must be opted out in settings. Full documentation (threat model, security spec) lives on an external docs site. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian stores notes as plaintext files on disk, so there is no built-in way to protect sensitive folders with a password while keeping Search, Graph and Backlinks working when unlocked.

relations.evidence: This plugin collects anonymous usage telemetry (via a self-hosted OpenPanel instance)

summary: Folder-level encryption tool that locks entire vault folders with AES-256-GCM and temporarily decrypts them for use during a session.
